hook: The most dominant athlete in the world is... a horse?
story: His name was Frankel, a British thoroughbred. Between 2010 and 2012 he ran 14 races and won all 14. He won the 2000 Guineas by six lengths - called one of the greatest displays ever seen on a British racecourse. Bookmakers eventually priced him at one-to-twenty: bet twenty to win one. The betting market simply gave up pretending he could lose.
number: Since 1948, the Timeform organisation has rated every racehorse. For nearly fifty years, the ceiling was 145. Frankel was rated 147 - the highest in the history of ratings.
closer: And the man training him, Sir Henry Cecil, was a racing legend the sport had written off - and he was dying of cancer. Frankel gave him fourteen wins on the way out; Cecil said one of them made him feel twenty years better. He died months after the horse retired.
full_text: The most dominant athlete in the world is... a horse? His name was Frankel, a British thoroughbred. Between 2010 and 2012 he ran 14 races and won all 14. He won the 2000 Guineas by six lengths - called one of the greatest displays ever seen on a British racecourse. Bookmakers eventually priced him at one-to-twenty: bet twenty to win one. The betting market simply gave up pretending he could lose. Since 1948, the Timeform organisation has rated every racehorse. For nearly fifty years, the ceiling was 145. Frankel was rated 147 - the highest in the history of ratings. And the man training him, Sir Henry Cecil, was a racing legend the sport had written off - and he was dying of cancer. Frankel gave him fourteen wins on the way out; Cecil said one of them made him feel twenty years better. He died months after the horse retired.
